lens: impact (demand x breadth x user-visible value, plus leverage for the factory). Checked read-only against upstream main ffc74885c5 (2026-10-01) with gh reads of issue and PR state and reactions. scores.rationale: This is a correctness defect in the patch tool, which nearly every coding session uses. The last-resort context_aware strategy (tools/fuzzy_match.py:261, per-line similarity >= 0.80) can apply an edit at the wrong anchor without any warning. #125376 shows 'trim()' matching 'strip()' at 0.923 on main. A silent wrong-region edit corrupts the user's code, which is worse than a failed edit, and CONTRIBUTING puts bug fixes first and asks to 'fail loud at integration boundaries'. The demand is a cluster of zero-reaction issues: #54572 (c=7) with carrier PR #54575, #125376, #111116, #111127, #93699, #124166, #125240 and #30962. Many independent reporters but few reactions. How often context_aware actually fires in real use is unmeasured, which is why this is not an 8.

scores.rationale: Every long session on the default local compressor goes through compaction. Losing identifiers there (ids, config keys, exact error strings) shows up to the user as forgetting and rework. The maintainer's own scorecards name summarizer identifier retention as the remaining gap. #122274 is a teknium-authored (harness-scout) issue, and #122522 is an open contributor carrier. The evals/compaction recall exam already exists and is accepted, so value can be shown in the maintainer's own currency. Demand from users is thin: #78457 (r=1), plus maintainer interest. Headroom is real but bounded: the 78.9% figure is a mean of 76.7, 90.0 and 70.0 across lineages, so a gain must be shown on a frozen lineage mix.
scores.corrections: Scope this to local-compressor routes. Native compaction (agent/native_compaction.py, opt-in codex_responses_native) keeps a local summary only whole and only up to RETAINED_SUMMARY_TOKEN_BUDGET = 32_000 (native_compaction.py:146), so a larger anchor index must keep summaries under that limit. #122522 (Nagisa-3000, summary_source=original) is a different mechanism that may compete or complement, so coordinate rather than duplicate. context_compressor.py is now 5,753 lines; _ANCHOR_PATTERNS is still at L1057.

scores.rationale: This has the strongest demand of any catalog feature. #39691 (headroom-ai tool-output compression, r=17, c=12) and teknium's #47866 evaluation report (r=27) show users care about tool-output token cost. teknium's 2026-09-23 harness-scout note on #107731 prescribes exactly this shape: a wire-only projection fired once per row at a compaction/prune boundary, with a cache-read ratio reported before and after, and with value resting on eviction, not recall. The benefit is token and cost reduction on long sessions, for every user on local routes. Two limits on the score: #47866 found lossless gains negligible and CCR net-negative, and the -30.3% Claude Code figure is only a prior.

Arms need both prune-off and prune-on baselines. #107731 is by lorencato23; it is a salvage, not ours. The teknium comment is a design note ('not a review verdict'), not an approval. Cache instruments already exist: evals/postmortem/live_ab/cache_concurrency_probe (~$50/arm, paid) or shared-metrics cache_break.count + model_tokens.sum (py3.14). The postmortem logcalls baseline undercounts misses until its cache= regex is fixed (logcalls.py:27-29 vs agent/turn_usage.py:192).

scores.rationale: The user-visible value is removing a 25-49 s stall (scorecard baseline $0.061 / 36.9 s per event) from inside the turn where compaction fires. Demand is moderate: #117886 (c=2), #76151, #79357 and #73468 (r=2 each), with open carrier #117895. The cost side is noise, per SCORECARD-2026-09-19, and a stall roughly once per ~150K tokens is noticeable but not dominant. Existing knobs may capture much of the value with no new code.

Measure critical-path seconds as post_auxiliary_call(aux_task='compression').api_duration. Regression guards: replay_gates, native_compaction/ab_checkpoint_preflight, cache_estimator_probe.
